land.text: the Song capital Kaifeng and its district, where the Jin installed Zhang Bangchang

predecessors.note: 'In 1127, the Jurchens installed a former Song official, Zhang Bangchang, as puppet emperor of the newly established Great Chu' (Jin-Song wars page). The Jin entered Kaifeng on 9 January 1127 (Jin page).

land.text: the Song capital Kaifeng and its district, where the Jin installed Zhang Bangchang

successors.note: 'After reigning for barely one month, Zhang Bangchang was persuaded by the Song to step down as emperor of the Great Chu' (Jin-Song wars page); 'the dynasty ended when Zhang agreed to recognize Emperor Gaozong as the new ruler' (Da Chu page). The Jin then fought for the plain again (see the northern-song dossier).

rulers.name: Zhang Bangchang
rulers.note: Infobox: reign 20 April 1127 to 23 May 1127; 'sentenced to death by being coerced into suicide on November 1, 1127' after submitting to Gaozong.

correction.text: the Song capital Kaifeng and its district, where the Jin installed Zhang Bangchang

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a state Cliopatria lacks. Reign 20 April to 23 May 1127 (Zhang Bangchang infobox); 'scarcely a month' (Da Chu page). The pages give no territory. The Da Chu and Zhang Bangchang pages name Jiankang (Nanjing) as Chu's capital, which no other page opened supports for a state installed by the Jin after Kaifeng fell; the shape is a 100 km disc round Kaifeng (confidence 1).

region.text: the Song capital Kaifeng and its district, where the Jin installed Zhang Bangchang

ledger.note: 20 April 1127: Zhang Bangchang is installed. Infobox 'Reign: 20 April 1127 - 23 May 1127'; 'In 1127, the Jurchens installed a former Song official, Zhang Bangchang, as puppet emperor of the newly established Great Chu' (Jin-Song wars page). The land is the researcher's reading (confidence 2): the pages say only that Jiankang was the capital.

region.text: the Song capital Kaifeng and its district, where the Jin installed Zhang Bangchang

ledger.note: 23 May 1127: Great Chu ends. 'The dynasty was abolished scarcely a month after its formation' (Da Chu page; Zhang and Empress Dowager Yuanyou agreed to recognize Gaozong). Zhang died on 1 November 1127.

certainty.note: One month of puppet rule; no page gives any territory.

sources.title: Zhang Bangchang
sources.note: Infobox reign 20 April to 23 May 1127, death on 1 November 1127.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks. The Da Chu and Zhang Bangchang pages say 'Jiankang, modern Nanjing, became the capital of Chu'; the Jin-Song wars and Jin pages have the Jin taking Kaifeng (entering it on 9 January 1127) and then installing Zhang, so the shape is a Kaifeng disc and no capital is entered. The Da Chu page's infobox lists the state 1127-1127; the Zhang page's infobox gives the day-level dates (20 April to 23 May 1127). The great-jin dossier's 1127 contest zone mentions 'Jin's puppets Chu and Qi' and has no vassal event for Chu; the northern-song dossier does not name this slug. The Jin-Song wars page's infobox gives Da Chu as 1127 and Da Qi as 1133-37.
